name: Ride a bike
blurb: If you never learned as a child, the balance-bike method gets adults riding in an afternoon — far faster than the running-behind-holding-the-saddle approach most people remember.
gear: A bike you can put both feet flat on the ground from
A gentle grassy slope or an empty flat car park
steps: Take the pedals off and drop the saddle so you can sit with both feet flat. This turns the bike into a balance bike and removes all the fear.
Scoot along, pushing with your feet, then lift both feet and glide. Practise gliding until you can go 10 metres with your feet up.
Learn to steer while gliding, and learn that you balance by steering into a lean, not by leaning.
Refit the pedals, raise the saddle slightly, and start with one pedal at the two-o-clock position to push off.
Practise starting and stopping repeatedly — those are the hard parts, not riding along.
Add looking over your shoulder, signalling and braking with both levers before going anywhere with traffic.
tips: Looking down at the front wheel makes you wobble. Look where you want to go, well ahead.
A saddle too high is frightening and a saddle too low is exhausting. Start low, raise it as confidence grows.
proof: You start unaided, ride 500 metres including turns, and stop under control.
